distinguishing_features: Uses impressed-current cathodic protection with a rectifier rather than barrier coatings or sacrificial-anode sizing.
Uses a high-output mixed-metal-oxide on titanium anode array.
Positions the anode array in the dry zone just above the maximum splash line instead of submerged.
Attempts to maintain cathodic steel potential during dry/thin-film phases at the wet-to-dry transition.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce corrosion of offshore splash-zone steel during cyclic wetting/drying, especially at oxygen-rich thin-film wet-to-dry transitions where conventional submerged protection paths become ineffective.
parsed.viable_reason: Cathodic protection requires a continuous ionic path, but an anode above the splash line may be unwetted and the candidate's lateral thin-film resistance is miscalculated, so holding the steel at the claimed potential in dry phases is physically unsupported.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The cited prior art is directed to chloride pulse dosing, impedance-based corrosion inference, and molybdate inhibitor dosing, and does not teach or suggest impressed-current protection of splash-zone steel using a dry-zone MMo/Ti anode array.
